name: Poporanism
summary: Poporanism is the Romanian peasant-centred populism developed by Constantin Stere and Garabet Ibraileanu from the 1890s to the 1910s. It sought a third path of development, neither capitalist nor Marxist, built on small peasant property, cooperatives, rural credit, land reform and universal suffrage, and it opposed revolution. It combined this with a strong cultural nationalism that treated the peasantry as the keeper of the Romanian spirit.
scope: The Romanian poporanist current around Constantin Stere's 'Social-Democratism or Poporanism?' (1907-08), the journal Viata romaneasca and Garabet Ibraileanu, as it existed at its peak before 1918 and in Stere's later peasantist politics. It excludes the Russian Narodniks, whom the poporanists distanced themselves from, and the later National Peasants' Party as a distinct organisation. The sources are thin on many issues, so most answers outside land, cooperatives, suffrage, Marxism, revolution and nationalism are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Garabet Ibraileanu
keyFigures.role: Critic and co-developer of poporanism around the journal Viata romaneasca

sources.title: Poporanism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, anti-capitalism and anti-Marxism, cooperatives, universal suffrage, nationalism and the split with Dobrogeanu-Gherea.

sources.title: Constantin Stere
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Stere's peasant state, land reform, suffrage, anti-revolutionary stance, monarchism, Bessarabia and WWI positions.

sources.title: The critical spirit in Romanian culture (Ibraileanu essay, with editorial context)
sources.author: Garabet Ibraileanu, in a Central European University Press volume
sources.usedFor: Ibraileanu's view of the peasantry as bearer of the national spirit, democracy as a means for nationalism, and the editors' account of Stere's middle-class and modernisation aims.

sources.title: Socialism in Romania in the 1900s
sources.author: Radio Romania International
sources.usedFor: Poporanism as a third path neither capitalist nor Marxist, cooperatives and rural banks, and the peasant question.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a documented issue for 1900s Romanian peasantists; inferred from their aim of raising peasant welfare through an active, reforming state and cooperative institutions.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage law was not a poporanist concern since the focus was a peasantry of smallholders, not wage labourers; adherents have no clear stance.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Poporanism sought a path that was neither capitalist nor Marxist and favoured cooperatives and state-backed rural credit, which suggests distrust of unregulated markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Stere's programme centred on private smallholdings plus cooperatives, not nationalised industry, yet he was no free-marketeer; nothing sourced on utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Stere attacked the large estates as the source of Romania's agrarian ills and wanted a broader middle class, so heavier burdens on big landowners are plausible but not documented.

unions-good.rationale: Stere judged the industrial proletariat too small to matter in Romania, so unions were peripheral; no documented stance.

property-fundamental.rationale: Poporanism defended small peasant property as the base of development, but also backed land reform against large owners, so property is not treated as untouchable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from the third-path anti-capitalist stance and preference for cooperatives and rural banks over unrestrained private capital.

cut-welfare.rationale: Poporanists wanted state action for peasants such as cooperative credit and amnesty, so welfare retrenchment fits poorly; welfare itself was not discussed.

worker-ownership.rationale: The collective ownership idea applied to peasant cooperatives, not workplaces generally; Stere explicitly warned against forced collectivisation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no basis for a position.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic issue for a 1900s agrarian movement; no basis for a position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anachronistic; poporanism was itself attacked with antisemitic smears but never legislated on speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Stere pushed universal suffrage and parliamentary reform and was loyal to the constitutional monarchy, which does not fit bypassing gridlock through a strongman.

state-harmful.rationale: Poporanists wanted a reforming "peasant state" with suffrage reform and cooperatives, so they plainly regard the state as necessary and useful.

limit-guns.rationale: Firearm regulation is absent from the sources on poporanism, and nothing in its agrarian programme points either way.

empower-police-military.rationale: Stere intervened in the 1907 revolt without calling the army and sought amnesty for rebels, implying distrust of coercive escalation.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A 1900s peasantist movement left sex work unaddressed; the source material gives nothing to infer from.

decide-locally.rationale: Stere later authored a 1929 decentralisation law, suggesting sympathy for local administration, though the peasant state was nationally driven.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy was not part of poporanist writing, though Stere's amnesty plea for the 1907 rebels hints at leniency.

traditional-family.rationale: The movement idealised rural communities that kept the national spirit; traditional family life is an inference from that rural romanticism.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the rural-traditional moral outlook of a 1900s Romanian movement.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the same rural-traditional orientation, with little documented.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement stressed national culture rather than religion; sources on it do not discuss religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial redress was not a Romanian issue of the era; the movement's concern was peasant class position.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sex and gender debate postdates the movement, so no position is documented or readily inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Poporanism championed the Romanian language and the preservation of the Romanian spirit, which Ibraileanu says the peasantry kept untouched.

gradual-change.rationale: Stere held that Romania needed no revolution and pressed reform through parliament and suffrage, though he also demanded sweeping land reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not an issue then; Stere's nationalism was cultural, so no clear position.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a nationalism focused on Romanian self-determination and anti-Russian foreign policy.

free-trade.rationale: Third-path economics aiming at national peasant development suggests scepticism of free trade; not explicitly documented.

nation-first.rationale: The movement's nationalism is described as pronounced, but statement concerns foreign policy trade-offs that sources do not cover.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Stere's foreign policy centred on Bessarabia and Russian expansion, not on intervening for human rights abroad.

open-borders.rationale: Pronounced nationalism and focus on the Romanian peasant nation make open borders unlikely, though not documented.

limit-growth.rationale: Poporanists supported modernisation, so a cap on growth does not fit; environmental issues were not raised.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is anachronistic for a movement from the 1890s to 1910s, so there is no basis for a lean.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Poporanists backed modernisation but prized rural community and were wary of simply importing Western models.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power postdates the movement entirely and nothing in its agrarian programme bears on it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Unlike the Narodniks, Stere did not think revolution was needed in Romania and favoured parliamentary reform; he warned forced collectivisation could breed Bolshevism.

experts-over-public.rationale: Ibraileanu gives intellectuals a guardian role over national morality and culture, but the movement pushed popular suffrage; overall leaning is against technocracy.

central-planning.rationale: Poporanism rejected Marxism and sought a non-capitalist path through peasant cooperatives, not central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cooperative farms in a market setting resemble this idea, but the statement mentions workers or public ownership generally; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Stere attacked large estates but the sources record no proposal to tax land value as a replacement for other taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from hostility to large estates and aim to widen smallholding; not documented.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional cash payments were not part of a programme built on peasant property and cooperatives.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Poporanists favoured agrarian development over industry; no stance on tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Poporanists supported limited state intervention per the sources, yet backed state-assisted credit and cooperatives; split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Stere wanted to strengthen small and medium peasant property and build a middle class, protecting small farms as the basis of development.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not a poporanist idea; inferred from preference for parliamentary democracy and voluntary cooperatives.

one-party-rule.rationale: Poporanists pursued universal suffrage and parliamentary reform; a ruling single party is contrary to that.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Stere stressed loyalty to the Romanian monarchy and worked within the constitutional monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: The movement supported voting rights for all, and Ibraileanu called democracy especially a means for nationalism; the "even when voters choose badly" clause is untested.

direct-votes.rationale: Stere sought universal suffrage for representative bodies; referenda are not documented.

workers-councils.rationale: Stere dismissed the industrial proletariat as too small to lead and favoured parliament reform.

right-to-secede.rationale: Stere's Bessarabian union work was about Romanian unification, and the movement's nationalism leans against secession rights.

natural-rulers.rationale: Poporanism was directed against aristocratic control of the peasantry and sought universal suffrage, so innate fitness to rule is rejected.

political-violence-never.rationale: No doctrine of absolute pacifism; Stere was anti-revolutionary but not pacifist.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nothing documented; Stere's WWI stance was strategic about Bessarabia, not a glorification of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion did not figure in the sources on the movement.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not a theme; the movement was secular-nationalist and reformist.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A movement seeking a reforming peasant state would not privatise courts or defence.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; Stere's foreign policy was about regaining Bessarabia.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nationalism was strongly cultural and linguistic, and Stere himself came from Bessarabia; ethnic exclusivity is not documented as a poporanist plank.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Poporanism opposed Marxism and Stere argued the proletariat was too small to drive Romanian change, rejecting a class-struggle reading.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Aimed at lifting peasants and creating a middle class, not equal outcomes; no stance.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The question of indigenous peoples' authority did not arise in the movement's Romanian context.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Romania had no overseas empire and the sources record no poporanist view on colonial reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; their nationalism was Romanian-specific.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Anti-capitalist third path and cooperative emphasis imply scepticism of self-interest as a moral ideal.

duties-before-rights.rationale: No documented stance; the movement was democratic yet communitarian about the nation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics lay outside the movement's interests; nothing in the sources addresses nature's intrinsic worth.

limit-population.rationale: Stere blamed estates and institutions for rural misery and the sources record no population policy.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Poporanists praised rural life but supported modernisation, so they were not hostile to industrial civilisation as a whole.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Backed modernisation but within a peasant-centred path, no documented stance on speeding disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement technology is anachronistic to the movement, so no position is available.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy is a modern question with no connection to the poporanist programme.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement supported modernisation and democratic reform rather than restoration, unlike the Samanatorists.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Poporanists were doctrinal about a peasant third path yet reformist in practice; sources show no stated view on pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Reform through parliament, party politics and suffrage rather than direct action; Stere worked inside the National Liberal Party.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources do not discuss this principle, though Stere's reformism over revolution is consistent with it.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement supported modernisation and rural cooperative farming, so a return to foraging is wholly alien.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; poporanist cooperatives aimed to gain large-scale production benefits, which accept specialisation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not a poporanist principle; they favoured peasant property.

production-for-use.rationale: Cooperative farms are consistent with this, but poporanists did not frame the economy this way.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Anti-capitalist yet opposed Marxist theory; no stated view on exploitation theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Poporanism opposed Marxism and Stere warned that imposing collectivisation could lead to Bolshevism.

collective-farming.rationale: Stere's cooperatives let smallholders share benefits without consolidating their land, and he warned against imposed collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Stere's war stance was strategic, and no sourced view on capitalism and imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: A reforming peasant state financing cooperatives and reforms cannot regard taxation as theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill-style limits on state coercion are not discussed in the sources on the movement.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement thought in terms of a peasantry and a national culture, favouring collective categories; not documented.

conscription.rationale: Stere backed a national war policy in 1914-18, but the sources record no stance on compulsory service itself.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement made voting rights for all its aim, so the vote matters more than exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Contradicts the idea of a peasant state serving social aims.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the push to give peasants the material means (land, credit, cooperatives) to escape aristocratic control.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources do not address who holds real political power, and universities and mass media were not poporanist targets.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not documented; Stere himself was the target of racist smears and the movement was cultural nationalist.

organic-representation.rationale: Poporanists demanded parliamentary reform and universal suffrage rather than corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: Culture was to be separated from politics per Stere, and the movement favoured limited state intervention.

national-rebirth.rationale: Concerned with modernisation and national spirit, but not a radical rebirth narrative.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Stere sought recovery and union of Bessarabia, a specific claim; general expansionism is not documented.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The movement sought to free peasants from aristocratic control, rejecting personal lordship.

bound-labor.rationale: Poporanism and Marxists alike aimed at emancipating the peasantry from neo-serfdom and aristocratic control.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Ibraileanu urged a critical spirit, but the sources give no poporanist view on the power-laden nature of knowledge.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; Ibraileanu urged a critical spirit rather than metaphysical claims.

single-common-good.rationale: The movement stressed peasant interests within a nation, but whether it saw a single rationally derived common good is not documented.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism is not discussed in the sources, and the movement's own antisemitism dispute concerned domestic Romanian politics.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed, though the Bessarabian cause suggests sympathy for co-nationals.

revive-national-language.rationale: The movement championed the Romanian language, but the statement is about reviving a lapsed language, an unaddressed case.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not discussed; cooperatives are democratic but concerned farms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from a reform-minded state-centred programme; not documented.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal doctrine was not part of the poporanist programme and sources record nothing on deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Anti-capitalist third path means they did not tie political freedom to economic liberty; they aimed at democracy through peasant welfare.

rule-by-example.rationale: Poporanists wanted legal and electoral reforms, not rule by rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Stere worked for the union of Bessarabia with Romania and resisted Russian expansion, an application of national self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN postdates the movement, so no stance on force without its approval can be drawn from the sources.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Ibraileanu urged an enlightened critical spirit, but religion is not discussed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility for immigrants was not an issue in rural Romania of the era and is undocumented.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare conditions are not discussed; the movement's concern was land and credit rather than benefit schemes.

class-collaboration.rationale: Poporanists sought a middle class between peasants and bourgeoisie and rejected class war, though landlords were opposed.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement championed preserving Romanian cultural heritage and spirit.

dominated-front.rationale: A common front of dominated countries against the West is a later idea; Stere's anti-Russian focus gives no direction.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism strong and rejecting Marxist internationalism, though a worker-specific stance was not documented.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gender roles are not documented in the sources, though rural-traditional sentiment may lean traditional.

ban-interest.rationale: The movement supported cooperative credit against moneylenders, but no ban on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Stere was a democrat favouring universal suffrage; racial classification contradicts that.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Opposed to Marxism and sought to use the state through reform to benefit peasants.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not part of the sources on a peasantist movement.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cultural nationalism hints at assimilation but unsourced.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred: the replacement conspiracy theory arose long after this reformist current, and nothing in its peasant-democratic programme points toward it.

national-mission.rationale: Poporanists rejected identification with Russian messianism; Romania was an emerging nation, so no mission to export is documented.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist structural analysis is not part of the movement's documented thought.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Ibraileanu describes the ruling class as stifling the productive elements; inferred as a critique of elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not documented; eugenics is anachronistic here.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed beyond Stere's amnesty for 1907 rebels.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wanted reforming state active in agrarian reform, credit, and suffrage.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Stere himself was targeted by racial smears; no support documented for such a policy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Universal suffrage implies equal civic standing, but not stated in terms of moral worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Stere denied socialism as an immediate goal and no internationalist doctrine.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The question of settler colonialism lies outside the movement's Romanian concerns.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal-law questions were not a poporanist theme in the sources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter bans have no place in Romanian peasant agriculture, which raised cattle for sale and food.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The sources on the movement do not discuss religious instruction in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxism was rejected, so the socialist-state doctrine has no place.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Universal suffrage and parliamentary reform express consent-based legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export targets are not in the sources, which describe a rural development focus.

population-transfer.rationale: Not documented; Stere himself was subject to ethnic smears.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Absolute non-aggression is a libertarian principle not discussed in poporanist sources.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Cooperative orientation and rejection of capitalism lean against struggle as progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Stere pursued suffrage and parliament, but the sources record no stance on banning anti-constitutional parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The aim of removing peasants from aristocratic control matches non-domination, though not so phrased.

separated-powers.rationale: Parliamentary reform was sought; separation of powers not discussed.

vanguard-party.rationale: Poporanism opposed Marxism, and Stere rejected revolution and proletarian leadership in Romania.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Focused on emancipating and raising the peasantry, the poor majority of Romania.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is anachronistic to the movement and nothing in the sources bears on it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law was marginal to a movement that regarded Romania's industrial working class as too small to matter.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Stere blamed large estates and social institutions for agrarian misery, not population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement's cultural nationalism might suggest a lean, but the sources contain no claim about diversity and cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sought representative elections and suffrage rather than lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Stere pressed for amnesty and avoided troops in 1907; he had a liberal-democratic record.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls on staple foods are not documented, though state support for peasant incomes was part of the outlook.

party-controls-media.rationale: A movement demanding voting rights for all and parliamentary reform stands against government control of information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Contrary to democratic aims and monarchic loyalty.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods are not discussed in the sources on the movement.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Stere sat in parliament as a regular politician, and the sources record no stand on representatives' pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not documented; Stere clashed with his own party and later left it.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Anachronistic; nationalism and anti-Russian outlook suggest scepticism.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Stere was loyal to the monarchy but pushed parliamentary reform; no stated view.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not covered in the sources on the movement.

clerical-rule.rationale: Stere's secular parliamentary reformism leaves no room for rule by senior religious scholars.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Stere favoured a national war policy (pro-Central Powers) and was nationalist; defeatism contradicts it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Ibraileanu urged a critical spirit and Stere separated culture from politics.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential terms are not an issue for a constitutional-monarchy reformer, and the sources record no stance.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not discussed in the sources, though Stere pursued parliamentary reform.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Stere advocated an alliance with the Central Powers in WWI.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: A forced end to renting has no source in poporanism, which dealt with rural landholding and not urban housing.

people-in-arms.rationale: Replacing the army with armed citizens is not documented; Stere's loyalty to the state and monarchy leans against it.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Poporanists praised rural communities as the keepers of the national spirit.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Stere campaigned for the union of Bessarabia with Romania and helped the 1918 vote.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Ibraileanu urges a critical intelligentsia; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural nationalism but no stance on hierarchy.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not discussed in the sources, though Stere's amnesty plea for 1907 rebels shows clemency.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education postdates the movement and is not discussed in the sources.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from an enlightened critical spirit.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Obscenity law is not covered in the sources on the movement.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Stere's Bessarabian unification work involved co-nationals, but the sources give no rule on citizenship transmission.

minority-language-support.rationale: The movement championed the Romanian language and national spirit; not documented.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions from general laws are not covered in the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument about conformity is not part of the documented poporanist outlook.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third World debt is anachronistic and no source records a poporanist view.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Poporanists treated national modernisation as requiring economic reform of the rural system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Parliamentary reform sought, but no documented stance.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Contradicts the demand for universal suffrage.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties lie outside the movement's national concerns in the sources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement entirely.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Stere stressed loyalty to the monarchy, and nothing in the sources addresses presidential election.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not addressed in the sources, which concentrate on land and cooperatives.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial compromise is not documented, though Stere's Bessarabia stance suggests attachment to claimed lands.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Backed land reform against large estates, suggesting property is subject to social purposes.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic, Stere warned against Bolshevism but no view on the label.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk doctrine postdates the movement.

collective-defense.rationale: Stere supported an alliance with the Central Powers, but the sources record no stance on collective-defence clauses.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations are not discussed in the sources on the movement.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Loyal to the monarchy as a constitutional institution; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The sources record nothing on using force against secession, and the movement's own nationalism pulls in unclear directions.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One-country-two-systems arrangements are not documented, though Stere's 1929 decentralisation law favoured regional administration.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A democratic movement with a constitutional monarchy outlook rejects divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from a reform programme aimed at raising peasants versus estate owners.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from the belief that peasants' condition stems from social institutions, not innate nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A programme of parliamentary reform and universal suffrage opposes a ruler unbound by law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space colonisation is wholly outside the movement's era and concerns.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-government theory is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

leader-cult.rationale: Personality cults contradict the democratic and parliamentary emphasis; Stere stressed loyalty to the monarchy only as an institution.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody doctrine is anachronistic to the movement and undocumented.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis that poporanists, who rejected Marxism, would not hold.

land-redistribution.rationale: Stere pushed land reform against large estates, which he held to be the source of Romania's agrarian problems, so distribution to the cultivators is central.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources record no view on refugees' right of return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Bessarabian claim rested on Romanian population, inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contrary to reformist and critical-spirit outlook.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not documented; inferred from secular outlook.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not documented and are anachronistic for a 1900s nationalist movement.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity of peoples sharing a language family is not documented beyond Romanian unification.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority self-government is not discussed in the sources, though the movement's own nationalism leaned toward Romanian cultural primacy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources contain nothing on minorities choosing between rights struggles and emigration.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Poporanism opposed Marxism and emphasised national spirit and culture.

ban-cartels.rationale: Anti-capitalist and pro-small-property outlook suggest support; unsourced.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescues are not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not documented; democratic but not majoritarian.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Stere favoured national development but not autarchic blocs; colonies are irrelevant.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Linked trade standards are modern and absent from the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacement of material incentives by social duty is a communist idea not discussed in poporanist sources.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Stere denied that revolution was necessary in Romania and sought parliamentary reform, so foco-style revolution is alien.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The movement sought to free peasants from aristocratic control, inferred to include privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cultural nationalism implies national history teaching, undocumented.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Romania was an emerging nation and the movement had its own tutelage concerns; not documented.

public-money-creation.rationale: The sources record no view on who should create money, though they mention cooperative banks and rural loans.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Stere argued Marxist predictions of proletarian impoverishment had failed, suggesting capitalism adapts, but he also rejected capitalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence in former imperial regions is not documented, apart from Stere's concern with Bessarabia.

delink-world-market.rationale: Poporanists admired Western models critically and favoured modernisation.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist concept absent from the sources on a movement that rejected Marxism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian freedom of private discrimination contradicts the movement's democratic egalitarian emphasis and support for state action.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional entrenchment is not discussed in the sources.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial boundary treaties were not part of the movement's concerns.

elective-rulers.rationale: Stere accepted monarchy while seeking parliamentary reform.

minority-veto.rationale: Consent-based minority vetoes conflict with a programme built on majority suffrage and reform legislation.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: A right of resistance is not discussed in the sources, though Stere stressed constitutional monarchy.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary reform was their aim, inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics lies outside the documented concerns of the movement.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Livestock farming was normal in the peasant economy, but the sources record no stance on animal welfare conditions.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The movement rejected aristocratic control, so noblesse oblige is not their solution.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Stere was a lifelong activist, party politician and parliamentarian, and the movement was a political programme.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of culture is not part of the sources on the movement.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is later than the movement, and sources show no view on global surplus transfer.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for the native-born is not documented, even though Stere himself, a Bessarabian refugee, held office in Romania.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns the Communist movement and does not apply to the anti-Marxist poporanists.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Poporanists sought a distinctively Romanian path to development, inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Stere's war stance centred on recovering Bessarabia from Russia.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The sources contain nothing on pre-colonial peoples' political leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism postdates the movement, so no position is available.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; Stere's warning on Bolshevism noted.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The US Civil War historiography debate has no link to the movement.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument disputes are modern and absent from the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's issues policy is anachronistic for the movement.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is anachronistic for the movement.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Ibraileanu argued Romania needed a critical spirit to choose what to borrow from the West, implying adaptation.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Stere handled the 1907 revolt without calling in the army, and a political guardian role for the military does not fit his civil reformism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Recognising domestic work as paid labour is a later feminist idea absent from the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service examinations are not discussed in the sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: A programme of national peasant-centred development suggests wariness of foreign control, but this is inferred, not documented.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates are not part of the documented programme, which sought parliamentary reform.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private pension accounts are anachronistic, and inferred opposition rests on the movement's anti-capitalist third-path outlook.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The movement defended private small peasant property, not communal tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The movement's goal of reforming parliament implies the principle that elected assemblies control spending, though this is not stated.

single-official-language.rationale: The movement championed Romanian but did not address minorities' languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign land ownership is not discussed, though nationalist peasantism may lean against it.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is a modern legal concept with no link to the movement.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism critiques are not documented for a movement of the early 1900s.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The sources contain no stance on arming foreign insurgents.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Stere resisted Russian domination, so imperial intervention is disfavoured.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign money are modern questions absent from the sources.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding rules for NGOs are modern and absent from the sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is not discussed in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases are not discussed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: The sources contain no stance on state employment guarantees.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Moral duty to obey law is not discussed; a reformist working inside parliament and a party is unlikely to deny it.

non-intervention.rationale: Absolute non-interference is not documented; Stere's concern with Bessarabia and Russia suggests a more nuanced foreign policy.

industrial-unions.rationale: Trade union structure was marginal for a movement focused on peasants.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Stere was himself smeared by antisemitic attacks and the Gherea split concerned antisemitism; the movement is not documented as promoting this.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Abolishing legal marriage is unlikely for a movement that praised rural community life, though this is inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information law is modern and absent from the sources.

local-production.rationale: Rural-cooperative economy suggests local orientation, inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Stere built his politics through newspapers, parties and parliament, not small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: International law supremacy is not discussed in the sources.

religious-nation.rationale: Poporanism's nationalism was linguistic and cultural, not religious.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Stere resisted Russian expansion, so ritual submission to a leading power is inferred as contrary to his stance.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not discussed, though Stere's 1929 decentralisation law concerned local administration.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The distinction between personal and productive property is Marxist and not framed in poporanist sources.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Delivery models for public services are not discussed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: This is a Marxist thesis; the poporanists opposed Marxism and praised the peasantry that kept the national spirit, though they did not discuss religion directly.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Poporanists rejected capitalism and sought a third path.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Women's equality was not part of the documented programme.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of childcare is not discussed in the sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: They championed Romanian but there is no evidence on loanword purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with nations inside a state are an Indigenous-law issue absent from the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cooperative farms fit, but communal property held in common does not; partial agreement.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement of the majority in minority regions is not documented in the sources.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The RRI source describes poporanism as a third path of development, neither capitalist nor Marxist.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Bessarabia claim leans on historical ties, inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The question postdates the movement, so this is an inference: Stere and the poporanists opposed antisemitism, and nothing in their record would support denying a later genocide.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The sources do not discuss sexual-offence law; the topic is anachronistic for the movement's literature.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Universal suffrage and parliamentary reform are incompatible with suppressing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The sources do not discuss blasphemy law, but Ibraileanu's call for an enlightened critical spirit leans against it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Romania had no colonies, and the movement's concern with peasants against exploiters leans against extractive rule.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic legal doctrine without a connection to the Romanian movement.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Takfiri rebellion is wholly alien to a movement that sought change by constitutional reform.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Universal suffrage and peasant empowerment, inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality postdates the movement and is not addressed in the sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Transgender legal recognition is anachronistic for the movement.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical end-of-life policy is anachronistic for the movement.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Poporanism called itself neither capitalist nor Marxist, which resembles a third way, but the sources give no stance on left-right as a frame.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept; the sources record no poporanist view on alienation under capitalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Islam in the West is a modern question with no link to the movement.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Dress rules in state institutions are not discussed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Modernising, reformist with cooperatives and limited state intervention, between capitalism and statism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Stere advocated an armed alliance and a national war aim in 1914-18, which is inconsistent with abolishing armies.

rich-first.rationale: Unbalanced-growth doctrine is not discussed in the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Stere argued for alliance with the Central Powers in the First World War rather than neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Stere stressed loyalty to the Romanian monarchy, which implies accepting dynastic succession for the head of state.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Cooperative credit and banks were part of the poporanist programme.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF-style austerity is anachronistic for the movement and absent from the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: Stere moved from census suffrage to universal suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is later than the movement.

reification.rationale: A Lukacsian Marxist concept not discussed in the poporanist sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Marxist critique of formal freedoms is not documented among poporanists, though they opposed aristocratic domination of peasants.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: A constitutional reformer seeking parliamentary reform would likely endorse rule through published laws, though this is not stated.

racial-franchise.rationale: Stere moved Romanian politics toward universal suffrage, which contradicts voting limited to one ethnic group.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data is modern and absent from the sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Marriage restriction is not documented; Stere's part in a movement that split from antisemitism leans against it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Gherea split over antisemitism; poporanists are not documented as promoting boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are a modern device absent from the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Concern at large estates dominating peasants.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Military service by gay people is anachronistic for the movement.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: A national movement praising the peasantry's preservation of the national spirit has no basis for promoting atheism, and state-led atheism is a Marxist-Leninist policy it rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Abolitionism is alien to a reformist movement that worked through parliament and the state.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational power-sharing is not discussed in the sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The movement wanted state-backed cooperatives, credit and land reform for peasants rather than reliance on charity.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a modern idea absent from the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Women clergy are not discussed in the sources.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital authority is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The movement's pronounced nationalism suggests reserving the vote to citizens, but this is inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps are not discussed; the movement concerned rural landholding.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property abolition is not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements are not documented; the movement favoured culture separate from politics.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign bases are not discussed, and the sources show Stere seeking alliances, not isolation.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Genocide recognition politics postdate the movement.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Peasant cultivators and the critique of estates, inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Absolute pacifism is not documented and Stere endorsed a national war aim, so killing in defence is likely accepted.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ibraileanu praised the peasantry as preserving the national spirit untouched.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Constructionist theory about sex is modern and absent from the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Martyr veneration is not documented in the sources, though pronounced nationalism may favour honouring the fallen.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Stere's secular, reformist politics treats politics as institutional reform and not as a cosmic battle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora homeland concepts are not discussed in the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: Ibraileanu's circle held that culture should be separated from politics, which gives no direction on sequencing national cultural renewal and statehood.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology of divine gender is anachronistic.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Economic nationalism favouring the ethnic majority is not documented.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Stere's work for union of Bessarabia with Romania suggests support for unifying a people in one unit, inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence is not discussed since the movement regarded industrial workers as marginal.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The test of socialism is not applied by poporanists, who rejected socialism as an immediate goal.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Municipal ownership of water and hospitals is not discussed.

second-chamber.rationale: Upper houses are not discussed in the sources, though Stere reported a single-college electoral reform.

municipal-property.rationale: Poporanists favoured private small peasant property and cooperatives rather than community ownership of the means of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Municipalist confederalism is not documented; Stere's reform ran through national parliament.

family-wage.rationale: Wage adequacy for family support is not discussed for a peasant-focused movement.

person-over-state.rationale: Personalist philosophy is not part of the documented movement.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The sources contain nothing about the spiritual dimension of politics.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Stere's decentralisation law, no stance on revocability.

dense-cities.rationale: The movement praised rural life as the keeper of national spirit, so favouring dense cities over the countryside is inferred as contrary.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Stere's movement organised by class (peasantry) and nation rather than race, and he suffered racial smears himself.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial pride is not addressed in the sources; the movement's pride was national and linguistic.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Stere's pro-Central Powers stance aimed to regain Bessarabia, an aim not clearly defensive, so adherents are not clearly committed either way.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Championed the Romanian language and spirit as the nation's core.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate religious electorates contradict the movement's goal of universal suffrage on a single register.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Stere feared Russian expansion, but the sources record no general partition-plot thesis.

free-public-college.rationale: University tuition policy is not discussed.

future-generations.rationale: Intergenerational environmental duties are not discussed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Difference feminism is not documented in the sources.

arms-reduction.rationale: Disarmament policy is not documented, and Stere pursued a national war aim.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Wilsonian open covenants are not discussed in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital flow policy is not documented, though third-path economics might incline to it.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A reformer working through the state and parliament would normally accept a state monopoly of arms, though this is not stated.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Stere backed a national war aim and the movement's nationalism contradicts refusing orders to fight.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wage bargaining was marginal for a movement centred on smallholder peasants.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits for low-paid families are modern and absent from the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Legal debt limits are not discussed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: A New International Economic Order is a later demand.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Stere rejected revolution and worked for change through parliament and the existing parties, which clearly implies taking over and reforming the state rather than destroying it; the source does not address the state-machine question directly.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Panarchist freedom to choose economic systems is not part of the programme, which prescribed a peasant path.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Internal colonialism theory is not documented, though the critique of landlords over peasants is somewhat analogous.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The sources do not address human nature.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Perennialism is not discussed in the sources.

farm-price-support.rationale: Cooperative farms, rural credit, and banks were central practical planks of poporanism, along with protecting smallholders.

workers-own-party.rationale: Before 1918 Stere argued that agrarian Romania was not ready for a separate social-democratic workers' party and led ex-socialists into the National Liberals; after 1918, though, he helped lead independent peasant parties and founded his own, so the stance shifted within the audit's scope.

ban-fgm.rationale: FGM is not discussed in the sources on a Romanian movement.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Women's property rights are not discussed in the sources.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The sources say nothing on the Romanian-Moldovan naming question, though Stere was a Bessarabian who championed Romanian language.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Libertarian tort remedies for pollution are anachronistic.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary chiefs are not relevant to the Romanian context.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental priority over liberty is anachronistic.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Immigrant language requirements are not discussed, though language championship suggests mild support.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Closed-shop questions are not part of a peasant-focused movement.

voter-id.rationale: Voter ID is modern and absent from the sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Religious law interpretation precedence is not discussed in the sources.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Procedural definition of democracy is not discussed in the sources, though universal suffrage was a goal.

premarital-sex.rationale: Sexual morality is not documented, although rural-traditional sentiment might lean conservative.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Negative income tax is a modern proposal absent from the sources.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Poporanists wanted cooperatives and rural banks within a monetary economy, so abolishing money wages is inferred as alien to them.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Stere's programme involved rural credit and banks but no documented view on central banking; adherents have no sourced position.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Stere sought Bessarabia's union via a 1918 vote, but sources record no general doctrine on annexation without consent.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-based admissions are anachronistic to a 1900s Romanian movement, so no position can be inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Poporanists campaigned for universal suffrage, but the sources speak of peasant men and never discuss women's votes; inferred as split for the period.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Poporanism treated the peasantry and its traditions as the keeper of the national spirit and did not criticize religion; inferred from that cultural nationalism.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not a documented issue for 1900s Romanian peasantists; their nationalism rested on culture and the peasantry rather than on racial theory, so no clear answer can be inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: State gender-equality bodies were anachronistic for the 1900s; inferred from the movement's focus on peasant land, credit and cooperatives, not women's policy.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not a documented poporanist position; inferred from their view that land belongs to the peasants who work it.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic for the period; inferred from Stere's liberal, pro-legal and pro-Entente outlook.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the rationalist, modernising outlook of Stere and Ibraileanu.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not documented; inferred from the movement's democratic, universal-suffrage reform outlook.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from poporanism's explicit rejection of Marxism and of state-led collectivism.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from their demand for universal suffrage, which implies direct popular voting rather than delegation.

national-church-status.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from their cultural nationalism that treats the peasantry's inherited traditions, including Orthodoxy, as the national spirit.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not documented; inferred from their Romanian cultural nationalism and centralised peasant state.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from Stere's Bessarabian roots and support for the self-determination of Romanians there.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic and not relevant to Romania's situation; no position can be inferred from the sources.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from their idealisation of the peasantry and its modest, self-reliant way of life as the national core.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not documented; inferred from their nationalism and focus on the Romanian peasantry.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the era's norm of male-only conscription, which they had no reason to challenge.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Poporanists treated the peasantry as keeper of the Romanian spirit and its small land holdings as the national base; the tie to land is inferred from that peasant nationalism.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Stere's push for legal reform and universal suffrage and his opposition to revolution.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Romanian national and Western-oriented cultural outlook of the movement.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Stere's nationalism and his concern for Romanians in Bessarabia and beyond the kingdom.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its land reform and small-property aims, which claim land for those who work it and not for large owners.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its defence of independent peasant smallholders against both capitalist and Marxist collectivisation.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from its aim of easing the burden on peasants; the sources do not mention consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from its aim of raising peasant welfare through cooperatives and rural institutions, a broad rather than means-tested approach.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from its stress on universal suffrage and an organised peasant state, which implies working through institutions rather than bypassing them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to capitalist and landowner elites, who it saw as exploiting the peasantry.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from a nationalism that unified Romanians across confession; not addressed directly.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from its third path of development, which combined modernising reform with respect for peasant tradition.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its reformist, modernising outlook, with low confidence.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from its economic nationalism and wish for an independent path of development.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from the poporanist programme of land reform and cooperatives to correct peasant poverty, which treats unequal outcomes as a problem whatever their origin; the sources do not discuss the question.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Anachronistic for 1900s Romania; poporanists distrusted finance capital but nothing documents a view on a transactions tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Anachronistic and not an issue for the movement; the ethnic question in Romania was treated mainly through nationalism and the peasant question, so no stance can be sourced.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from poporanists' gradualist, anti-revolutionary commitment to reform through suffrage and legal institutions, which favours changing unjust laws rather than disobeying them.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from their small-property, peasant-centred economy and wariness of industrial capitalism; the sources do not address automation, which is anachronistic.

multipolar-world.rationale: Anachronistic; poporanist cultural nationalism favours national independence of development, but no source states a view on the world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Stere's critique of Marxism rejected its schema for Romania, but the sources do not say whether poporanists accepted the labour theory of value; peasant labour was central to their thinking.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Poporanism fused cultural nationalism with a politics for the peasantry, who were seen as the keepers of the national spirit, so love of country and serving the working rural masses belong together.

material-over-identity.rationale: The statement is about a modern left; poporanists combined material peasant welfare with strong cultural and national identity, so the contrast does not fit and no answer can be sourced.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Poporanism rejected both Marxism and revolution and sought a peasant path under universal suffrage, so a market economy under communist party leadership is foreign to it.

missingStatements.text: Small family farms organised in cooperatives are the best basis for a country's economic development.
missingStatements.rationale: Stere proposed a peasant state protecting small farms, with cooperatives giving smallholders the gains of large-scale production without merging their land.

missingStatements.text: Intellectuals should act as guardians of the nation's culture and morality, kept separate from party politics.
missingStatements.rationale: The editors' account of the movement says culture was to be separated from politics, with intellectuals as guardians of national morality.
missingStatements.declined: Rare position held by few ideologies; intellectuals' role is captured loosely by experts-over-public.

notes: Sources on poporanism are mostly short or secondary; the primary text used is an Ibraileanu essay excerpt, not Stere's 1907-08 essay itself. Most answers are therefore low-confidence inferences. Poporanism had cultural-nationalist strands (Ibraileanu) and a political-reformist one (Stere in the National Liberal and peasantist parties).
